title: Invariant closed support base-change identification
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $A=A_{E,n}$ as in [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $X,C$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_kX$ an admissible correspondence of [def-trf-correspondence]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed reduced subscheme with complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and assume $c_2(c_1^{-1}Z)\subseteq Z$ set-theoretically. Work on the small etale sites, with the bounded constructible finite-Tor categories identified with their pro-etale counterparts by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. Put $W=C\times_{c_1,X}Z$ and $Y=W_{\mathrm{red}}$, and let $h_Z:Y\hookrightarrow C$ be the induced closed immersion. The two maps $c_1h_Z,c_2h_Z$ factor uniquely through $i$, giving $d_1,d_2:Y\to Z$. For $T=Rc_{1!}c_2^*$ and every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, compact-support base change followed by the reduction equivalence gives a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\theta_K:i^*TK\xrightarrow{\sim}Rd_{1!}d_2^*i^*K.$$
Define $K_U=j_!j^*K$ and $K_Z=Ri_*i^*K$ with localization arrows $a:K_U\to K$ and $b:K\to K_Z$, respectively the counit for $j_!\dashv j^*$ and the unit for $i^*\dashv Ri_*$. Then $i^*T(a)=0$ and $i^*T(b)$ is an isomorphism, compatibly with the displayed natural base-change identification.
